chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah support him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Abū ʿAlī al-Ashʿarī, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār and Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān, all together from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Ibn Muskān, from al-Ḥasan ibn Ziyād al-Ṣayqal, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
"One fresh palm stalk is placed for the deceased on the right, and the other on the left." He said, and he said: "The palm stalk benefits the believer and the disbeliever."

key_terms.الْيَسَارِ: the left side of the deceased
key_terms.الْيَمِينِ: the right side of the deceased
key_terms.جَرِيدَةٌ: a fresh palm stalk placed with the dead

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about placing palm stalks with the deceased?
ai.summary: This hadith states the practice of placing two fresh palm stalks with the deceased, one on the right side and one on the left side. It further states that this act brings benefit to both the believer and the disbeliever, indicating its significance in the rites connected to burial and the state after death.
